# 1. Create synthetic dataset 1 for testing
Simple associations but no interactions
## a. Define covariates
```{r}
# Define number of individuals
n_subjects <- 200

# Simulate covariates: e.g., a binary treatment variable (trt) and age
set.seed(123)
covariates <- data.frame(
  id = 1:n_subjects,
  surgery = rbinom(n_subjects, 1, 0.6), # 60% chance of surgery
  chf = rbinom(n_subjects, 1, 0.2), # 20% chance of chf
  s_age = rsn(n = n_subjects, xi = 0, omega = 1, alpha = 4)   # Standardised age in months as skew-normal distribution
)

```


## b. Generate true survival times
```{r}
# Define the true parameter values (log hazard ratios for covariates)
# The 'names' correspond to column names in the 'covariates' data frame
betas <- c(surgery = -0.5, s_age = 0.03, chf = 2.0)

# Define the shape (gamma) and scale (lambda) parameters for the baseline Weibull distribution
# Note: 'simsurv' uses 'gammas' for shape and 'lambdas' for scale
# Setting gamma=1 results in an exponential distribution
gammas <- c(shape = 0.75)
lambdas <- c(scale = 0.01)


# Simulate event times
set.seed(123)
true_event_times <- simsurv(
  dist = "weibull",
  x = covariates,
  betas = betas,
  gammas = gammas,
  lambdas = lambdas
)

# Combine with covariates for a complete dataset
sim_data <- merge(covariates, true_event_times, by = "id")
sim_data <- sim_data |>
  mutate(centre = sample(x = LETTERS[1:3], size = n_subjects, replace=TRUE))
```



## c. Incorporate censoring
```{r}
# Define a maximum follow-up time (e.g., 5 years)
max_follow_up <- 3000

# Simulate a random censoring time (e.g., uniform distribution up to max_follow_up)
# The actual censoring time could also be dependent on other factors
set.seed(123)
sim_data$censor_time <- runif(n_subjects, 0, max_follow_up)

# Determine observed time and event status
sim_data$time <- pmin(sim_data$eventtime, sim_data$censor_time)
sim_data$status <- as.numeric(sim_data$eventtime <= sim_data$censor_time) # 1 = event, 0 = censored
```



## d. Generate data summary of synthetic data 1
```{r}
sumtable(sim_data)
```





# 2. Create synthetic dataset 2 for testing

Simple associations with interaction of chf on clinical_signs
## a. Define covariates
```{r}
# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Define number of individuals
n_subjects <- 250

prob_impact <- 0.75 # Probability of 'impacted' being 1 when 'influencer' is 1
prob_no_impact <- 0.25 # Base probability of 'impacted' being 1 when 'influencer' is 0


# Create the Influencing Variable (chf)
# Simulate a binary variable (0 or 1)
chf = rbinom(n_subjects, 1, 0.5) # 50% chance of chf


# Create the Impacted Variable (clinical_signs) ---
# Use case_when to create Y based on X, with controlled probabilities
clinical_signs <- case_when(
  chf == 1 ~ rbinom(n_subjects, 1, prob_impact), # If influencer is 1, Y has high chance (75%) of being 1
  chf == 0 ~ rbinom(n_subjects, 1, prob_no_impact) # If influencer is 0, Y has low chance (25%) of being 1
)


# Simulate covariates: e.g., a binary treatment variable (trt) and age

covariates2 <- data.frame(
  id = 1:n_subjects,
  chf = chf,
  clinical_signs = clinical_signs
)

```


## b. Generate true survival times
```{r}
# Define the true parameter values (log hazard ratios for covariates)
# The 'names' correspond to column names in the 'covariates' data frame
betas2 <- c(clinical_signs = 0, chf = 0.75)

# Define the shape (gamma) and scale (lambda) parameters for the baseline Weibull distribution
# Note: 'simsurv' uses 'gammas' for shape and 'lambdas' for scale
# Setting gamma=1 results in an exponential distribution
gammas <- c(shape = 0.4)
lambdas <- c(scale = 0.01)


# Simulate event times
set.seed(123)
true_event_times2 <- simsurv(
  dist = "weibull",
  x = covariates2,
  betas = betas2,
  gammas = gammas,
  lambdas = lambdas
)

# Combine with covariates2 for a complete dataset
sim_data2 <- merge(covariates2, true_event_times2, by = "id")
sim_data2 <- sim_data2 |>
  mutate(centre = sample(x = LETTERS[1:3], size = n_subjects, replace=TRUE))
```



## c. Incorporate censoring
```{r}
# Define a maximum follow-up time (e.g., 5 years)
max_follow_up <- 3000

# Simulate a random censoring time (e.g., uniform distribution up to max_follow_up)
# The actual censoring time could also be dependent on other factors
set.seed(123)
sim_data2$censor_time <- runif(n_subjects, 0, max_follow_up)

# Determine observed time and event status
sim_data2$time <- pmin(sim_data2$eventtime, sim_data2$censor_time)
sim_data2$status <- as.numeric(sim_data2$eventtime <= sim_data2$censor_time) # 1 = event, 0 = censored
```



## d. Generate data summary of synthetic data 2
```{r}
sumtable(sim_data2)
```

# 3. Check effects in dataset 1
# I.  Bayesian Cox's regression for EFFECT OF SURGERY (surgery y/n) with random intercept for centre

## Informative prior for surgery
### i. surgery
Set a non_informative weakly regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2)


```{r}
prior_surgery <- student_t(df = 3, 
                           location = 0,
                           scale = 2,
                           autoscale = FALSE)
```


 

## Fit model with for surgery
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_sx <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ 1 + surgery +  (1| centre),
  data = sim_data,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior = prior_surgery,
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 2000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```



## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_sx)
```



## Model summary
```{r}
summary(mod_sx)
```



## Model short summary
```{r}
print(mod_sx, digits = 3)
```




##  Plot Baseline hazard of model
```{r}
plot(mod_sx)
```



## Plots of model convergences

## Get results
```{r}
posterior_mod_sx <- as.array(mod_sx)
```



### a. Check trace plots for model
```{r}
color_scheme_set("mix-blue-pink")
mcmc_trace(posterior_mod_sx)
```



### b. Trace rank plot
```{r}
mcmc_rank_overlay(posterior_mod_sx)
```



### c. get dens overlay plot for chains
```{r}
color_scheme_set("blue")
mcmc_dens_overlay(posterior_mod_sx)
```



## Summaries of coefficients

### HPDI for the different beta parameters
```{r}
draws <- as.matrix(mod_sx)
median(draws[,2]) # 2nd column is draws for surgery
HPDI(draws[,2], 0.97) # 2nd column is draws for surgery
HPDI(draws[,2], 0.89) # 2nd column is draws for surgery
```



### Hypothesis tests on beta parameters
#### surgery
probability that effect is negative
```{r}
mean(draws[,2] < 0) # 2nd column is draws for surgery
```



### a. Get HDI for coefficients
```{r}
hdi <- bayestestR::hdi(mod_sx, ci = c(0.50, 0.68, 0.89, 0.97), parameters = "surgery")
plot(hdi)
```



## Get density plots for posterior distributons of beta parameters
```{r}
mcmc_dens(posterior_mod_sx,
  pars = c("surgery"))
```



## Get area plot for posterior distributons of beta parameters
```{r}
mcmc_areas(posterior_mod_sx,
  pars = "surgery")
```



## Calculate hazard ratios for surgery
### a. get posterior draws
```{r}
surgery_hr <- exp(draws[,2]) # 2nd column is draws for surgery)
```



### b. Summarise hazard ratios for surgery
```{r}
median(surgery_hr)
hdi_surgery_hr <- hdi(surgery_hr, ci = c(0.50, 0.68, 0.89, 0.97))
hdi_surgery_hr
```



### c. Plot posterior distribution for hazard ratio of surgery
```{r}
ggplot(data.frame(surgery_hr), aes(x = surgery_hr)) +
  geom_density(fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Posterior distribution of hazard ratio for surgery",
       x = "Hazard Ratio",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype="dotted", 
                color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.5)
```



## Check model performance
### check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_sx) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```



### check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_final_prior_only <- update(mod_sx, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_final_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```



## Make model predictions and plot for surgery
### create new data where age differs
```{r}
nd <- data.frame(centre = rep("A", 2),
                 surgery = c(0, 1)
                 )
head(nd)
```



### make posterior predictions from new data
```{r}
ps <- posterior_survfit(mod_sx,
  newdata = nd,
  times = 0,
  extrapolate = TRUE,
  control = list(edist = 5)) |>
  suppressWarnings()
head(ps)
```



### plot
```{r}
panel_labels <- c('1' = "No surgery", '2' = "Surgery performed")
pps <- plot(ps) +
  aes(colour = factor(id), fill = factor(id)) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.95, 1.0)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels))
print(pps)
```



## Check PH assumption visually
### make predictions of both the hazard and log hazard
```{r}
ph <- suppressWarnings(posterior_survfit(mod_sx, newdata = nd, type = "haz"))
pl <- suppressWarnings(posterior_survfit(mod_sx, newdata = nd, type = "loghaz"))

```



#### create plots
```{r}
pph <- plot(ph) +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels))
ppl <- plot(pl) +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels))
```



#### combine plots in grid and plot
```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 8}
plot_grid(pph, ppl, ncol = 1)
```



## Create KM curve
```{r}


# Basic KM curve for the entire dataset
km_strat <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1 + surgery, data = sim_data)

# Convert to tidy format
km_df <- broom::tidy(km_strat)


# Columns: time, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, strata, n.risk, n.event, n.censor
ggplot(km_df, aes(x = time, y = estimate, colour = strata, fill = strata)) +
  geom_step() +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Time",
    y = "Survival probability",
    colour = "Surgery",
    fill = "Surgery",
    title = "Kaplan–Meier curves stratified by surgery"
  )
```



## Fit frequentist Cox PH model for effect of surgery
```{r}
# Fit Cox PH model
freq_cox_sx <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ 1 + surgery + strata(centre),
  data = sim_data)

summary(freq_cox_sx)
```

# 4. Check effects in dataset 2

## Informative prior for chf

### i.chf
As chf is associated with a HR of 4.8
Set a non-informative weakly regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2)



```{r}
prior_chf2 <- student_t(df = 3,
                       location = 0,
                       scale = 2,
                       autoscale = TRUE)
```



## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_chf2 <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ 1 + chf + (1| centre),
  data = sim_data2,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior = prior_chf2,
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 2000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

```{r}
                       autoscale = TRUE)
```



## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_chf3 <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ 1 + chf + (1| centre),
  data = sim_data3,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior = prior_chf3,
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 10, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 2000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

#      AND also for the DIRECT EFFECT of CHF
Here, we adjust for the effect of CHF by stratifying on that variable

## Non-informative prior for clinical_signs

```{r}
                           location = 0,
                           scale = 2,
                           autoscale = FALSE)
```

NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_clin_si_true3 <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ 1 + clinical_signs + chf + (1| centre),
  data = sim_data3,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior = prior_clin_si_chf,
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 10, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 2000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```
